title: 🏛️ Exams 2002–2026 · building the comparison: -er, -est, more, as … as ⭐⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021, general) A text about shopping online says: "There are a few problems that customers face while shopping online. The ___ one is that you have no guarantee of a product's quality." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The text speaks of a few problems and picks the one at the top of the list, so it needs the superlative of the short adjective "big": the + biggest, with a double g. "Bigger" compares only two things, "biggerest" marks the degree twice, and "more big" is not a form of a short adjective.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2016, general) A text about a travelling library says: "Soriano created a travelling library for the inhabitants of his town. When asked if he would move to a ___ city, he said 'I don't think so. My place is here.'" Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The writer compares the city with his own town, so it is a comparison between two places: the comparative of the short adjective "big", with a double g and the ending -er. "Biggest" is a superlative and cannot follow "a", "more big" uses "more" with a short adjective, and "more bigger" marks the comparison twice.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2015, general) A text about a camp for children who spend too much time on the Internet says: "Children at the camp are computer addicts. That's why they are encouraged to spend ___ much time as possible outdoors." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The expression is "as much ... as possible": the first "as" opens the equality and the second one closes it. "So", "than" and "more" cannot open this fixed expression. After "as much" the phrase always closes with "as", never with "than".

questions.prompt: (Exam 2011, general) A text about reducing air pollution says: "Walk or ride a bicycle for short trips, or take public transport for ___ ones." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The clue is "short trips": the sentence opposes short trips to longer ones, with the comparative of the short adjective "long" (-er). "Faster" is a comparative but it does not oppose "short", "longest" is a superlative, and "more long" uses "more" with a short adjective.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2009, general) A paragraph on waste explains what parents should teach: "As parents, our role is to teach the next generations that it is not necessary to have the ___ model of everything." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The model is compared with every other model of everything, so the superlative of the short adjective "new" is needed after "the": the newest, with no change of spelling. "Newer" compares only two things, "most newest" marks the degree twice, and "more new" is not a form of a short adjective.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2005) A wildlife text gives the maximum height of an adult giraffe: "... up to 6 meters ___ ." Choose the correct form of the adjective.
questions.explanation: After a measurement the adjective keeps its plain form: 6 meters tall. Nothing is compared in this sentence: there is no "than", no "as ... as" and no group of animals. So an -er ending, an -est ending or "more" are all out of place.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025, general) A text about teenagers and technology says: "That's mainly because they meet-up online. It's far (fashionable) ___ to chat online than meet-up!" Put the word in brackets in the right form. Type the missing words.
questions.explanation: "Fashionable" has four syllables, so it is a long adjective: the comparison is made with a word placed before it, not with an ending, and the sentence goes on with "than" because two ways of meeting are compared. An -er ending or a superlative form would both be wrong here.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2026, general) A text about "democratic learning" says that the students "are also encouraged to listen to their own ___ and most compassionate voices". Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The clue is "and most compassionate": the two adjectives are joined, so both are superlatives, the top of all the voices. "Wise" is short and ends in -e, so it only adds -st: wisest. "Wiser" is a comparative, "wiseest" adds a second e, and "more wise" is a comparative with the wrong form for a short adjective.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2016, technical) A text about mechanics says: "In smaller garages or companies, a mechanic must be familiar with all of these systems. In ___ garages, however, technicians must be able to use a range of tools like jacks and screwdrivers." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The clue is "smaller" in the sentence before and "however": the second sentence opposes the small garages to the big ones, so it needs the opposite comparative of the short adjective "large": larger. "Largest" is a superlative, "colder" is a comparative that does not oppose "smaller", and "more large" uses "more" with a short adjective.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2015, general) At the same camp the children swim, do aerobics and eat a healthy lunch, and many promise to limit the time they spend on their computers at home. "Children who attend the camp say they feel much ___ by the end of it." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The camp helps the children, so they feel better, the comparative of "good". This adjective has its own irregular comparative: it does not take -er or "more". "Worse" is the comparative of "bad" and would say the opposite of what the camp achieves, and "gooder" and "more good" apply the regular rules to a word that does not follow them.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2006) A text about sharing housework says: "Many husbands don't mind giving a hand but others would never like to do the ___ routines like the washing-up or the ironing." Which word completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The word "the" and a whole group of routines call for the superlative. "Easy" is a short adjective that ends in a consonant + y, so the y becomes i: easiest. "Easyest" forgets this spelling rule, "most easy" uses "most" with a short adjective, and "more easy" is a wrong comparative.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2002) A text calls tigers magnificent animals: "They are the ___ meat-eating animals ..." The sentence ends by saying where they live. Which word fits the gap?
questions.explanation: Tigers are compared with all the other meat-eating animals on land, so the sentence needs the superlative of the short adjective "large": the + largest, with only an -st because the word already ends in -e. "Larger" compares two things, "most large" uses "most" with a short adjective, and "most largest" marks the degree twice.
